questions.question: Explain how a street light switches on and off by itself, and describe its input, process and output.
questions.expected_answer: A light sensor on top acts as an automatic switch. When daylight fades, it completes the circuit and the light comes on; in the morning it breaks the circuit and the light goes off. Input: electrical energy and a signal from the sensor. Process: the circuit is completed through the wires. Output: light.

questions.question: Describe how an alarm and an electric gate work as systems.
questions.expected_answer: In an alarm, switches or sensors on doors and windows change the circuit when a door opens or someone moves, and the control box sets off a siren and lights as a warning. In an electric gate, a remote control sends a signal to a receiver, the control box completes the circuit to an electric motor, and the motor moves the gate along a track; sensors stop it at the end or if something is in the way.

questions.question: What problems do fans and heaters solve, and which component gives the output in each?
questions.expected_answer: Fans solve the problem of feeling too hot: a motor turns the blades, which move air and help sweat evaporate to cool us. Heaters solve the problem of cold rooms: a heating element gets very hot when electricity flows through it and gives off heat. A thermostat can switch a heater off when the room is warm enough.
